definition: Confluence means a flowing together of separate streams, forces, or events into one.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word confluence. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know confluence should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Ask the ranger why the wildflowers exploded this June and she names a confluence — wet winter, cool spring, and last summer's burn.
An intersection stops short of a confluence — the roads touch at one point and go their own ways, each unchanged, while a confluence joins separate streams into one shared flow.
Fusion goes further than confluence — merged streams still carry two waters in one bed, but fused things have become a single substance with no seam.

Convergence names the approach — separate paths still bending toward one point, a meeting promised but not yet made. A confluence is what convergence becomes at the meeting itself: the joined flow, separate currents now moving on together as one.

A junction is the fixed place where routes meet — a dot on the map, pure geography. A confluence is not a place but a happening: separate streams or forces actually flowing together into one. You can stand at a junction; a confluence carries you along.
